narration_timeline.text: Why does a city pigeon suddenly stop pecking at food and take off?
narration_timeline.scene: Authentic urban pigeons pecking at food.

narration_timeline.text: A flock searches the ground for food while keeping track of nearby movement.
narration_timeline.scene: A pigeon on an urban station platform, not misrepresented as feeding.

narration_timeline.text: When something nearby startles a pigeon, it can suddenly spring into the air in a flash.
narration_timeline.scene: One genuine pigeon flushing and a separately filmed cat chasing another pigeon; never imply a single incident.

narration_timeline.text: That quick departure creates distance from a possible threat, including a nearby cat.
narration_timeline.scene: Real rock pigeon close view, explanation of escape mechanism as voice-over.

narration_timeline.text: But once the disturbance passes, pigeons can settle back into their ordinary routines.
narration_timeline.scene: Close real pigeons feeding in an urban park; narration does not claim the footage is from the same disturbance.

narration_timeline.text: The burst of wings is a fast escape, not the end of the bird's search for its next meal.
narration_timeline.scene: Real pigeons eating bread and a separately filmed group on a pier.
